changes.current_line: Recover failed payments automatically with smart retries.
changes.change: For membership and subscription businesses that report churn to their board: "Split your churn into members who cancelled and members whose card just failed. Then win back the members who never meant to leave, automatically." Keep smart retries as the how, not the headline.
changes.why: The evaluation began as a board-level churn problem, and failed payments only mattered once churn was split, so the customer's phrase "members who never meant to leave" names the problem in their terms rather than ours.

changes.current_line: Proven ROI, backed by an independent economic impact study.
changes.change: For recovery deals, especially when finance signs: "Send us one month of your failed renewals. We'll show you which ones usually come back with a retry or an updated card, and give you the spreadsheet to keep." Lead with their file, not our average.
changes.why: What landed was an analysis of the customer's own failed renewals ("Their file, not our average."); the silent controller asked for the spreadsheet, and the deal was signed four days later.

changes.current_line: Online and in-store on one platform; the line between them has pretty much disappeared.
changes.change: Do not lead with "unified commerce" or the one-platform claim for in-store prospects whose studio or front-desk software we support only through a partner integration. Instead, name the supported front-desk software and show a live demo of check-in and sale in that software before claiming in-store.
changes.why: When the rep said "unified commerce", the champion asked "is that the readers?"; we couldn't show the reader working inside their studio software, and the front desk stayed with the incumbent.

changes.current_line: Financial infrastructure to grow globally, in every currency.
changes.change: Do not open with the global positioning line for prospects operating in one or two countries. Open with the business problem they already track, for example churn, instead.
changes.why: The rep opened with the global slide and got silence from a customer with studios in the US and a handful in Canada.
